## spectral.kt { #spectral-kt }

Frequency-domain / spectral analysis family for the stdlib DSP toolkit.

This is the frequency-domain companion to `timeseries.kt` (which is entirely time-domain).
It is self-contained and additive: a pure-Kotlin FFT, analysis windows, a [`Spectrum`](math.md#spectral-kt-spectrum) and a
[`Spectrogram`](math.md#spectral-kt-spectrogram) (STFT), classic spectral features (centroid / spread / rolloff / flux / flatness /
RMS / energy), and streaming [`FloatFilter`](math.md#timeseries-kt-floatfilter) wrappers so the spectral features drop straight into
the existing time-domain filter chain in `timeseries.kt` (compose with `then`).

Everything is plain `Double`/`Float` math — no external DSP dependency — so it works headless in
a box, a test, or a docs capture. The FFT is an iterative Cooley–Tukey radix-2 core with a
Bluestein (chirp-z) fallback so arbitrary (non-power-of-two) lengths transform exactly.

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/stdlib/spectral.kt`

**Used in:** [Spectral examples](../spectral_examples.md)

### Top-level functions { #spectral-kt-functions }

| Declaration | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">fun</span> <span class="nf">fft</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">signal</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">DoubleArray</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">sampleRate</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Double</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="n">signal</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="n">size</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="nf">toDouble</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Spectrum</span></code><span class="sig-overloads">+2 overloads · also FloatArray, List&lt;Float&gt;</span> | Forward FFT of a real signal. `sampleRate` defaults to the signal length (bins == cycles/frame). |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">fun</span> <span class="nf">fft</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">signal</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">DoubleArray</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">window</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">WindowType</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">sampleRate</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Double</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="n">signal</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="n">size</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="nf">toDouble</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Spectrum</span></code> | Windowed forward FFT: multiplies by `window` first (amplitude compensated by coherent gain). |

| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">fun</span> <span class="nf">stft</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">signal</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">DoubleArray</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">fftSize</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mi">1024</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">hopSize</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="n">fftSize</span> <span class="p">/</span> <span class="mi">4</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">window</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">WindowType</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="nc">WindowType</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="nc">HANN</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">sampleRate</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Double</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="n">signal</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="n">size</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="nf">toDouble</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Spectrogram</span></code><span class="sig-overloads">+2 overloads · also FloatArray, List&lt;Float&gt;</span> | Short-time Fourier transform. Frames of `fftSize` samples are windowed by `window` and advanced by `hopSize`; the tail is zero-padded so the final partial frame is kept. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">fun</span> <span class="nf">istft</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">spec</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Spectrogram</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">DoubleArray</span></code> | Inverse STFT — weighted overlap-add reconstruction of a real signal from a [`Spectrogram`](math.md#spectral-kt-spectrogram). Each frame is inverse-transformed, re-windowed (synthesis window == analysis window) and overlap-added; the running window-energy is divided out so a Hann-windowed COLA STFT reconstructs faithfully. |

### FFT { #spectral-kt-fft }

<code class="highlight"><span class="k">object</span> <span class="nc">FFT</span></code>

The transform itself: an in-place, self-contained complex FFT that accepts **any** length, not just a power of two.

| Declaration | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">fun</span> <span class="nf">isPowerOfTwo</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">n</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Boolean</span></code> | True for 1, 2, 4, 8, … — and false for zero and negatives, so it is safe on unvalidated input. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">fun</span> <span class="nf">nextPowerOfTwo</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">n</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span></code> | Smallest power of two >= `n` (>= 1). |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">fun</span> <span class="nf">transform</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">re</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">DoubleArray</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">im</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">DoubleArray</span><span class="p">)</span></code> | Forward FFT in place. `re`/`im` must be the same length; any length >= 1 is accepted (power-of-two goes through the radix-2 kernel, otherwise Bluestein). |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">fun</span> <span class="nf">inverseTransform</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">re</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">DoubleArray</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">im</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">DoubleArray</span><span class="p">)</span></code> | Inverse FFT in place, **normalized** (divides by N). By the standard identity the inverse is the forward transform with real/imag swapped, then scaled by 1/N. |

| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">fun</span> <span class="nf">transformBluestein</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">re</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">DoubleArray</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">im</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">DoubleArray</span><span class="p">)</span></code> | In-place arbitrary-length forward transform via Bluestein's chirp-z algorithm. |

### WindowType { #spectral-kt-windowtype }

<code class="highlight"><span class="k">enum</span> <span class="k">class</span> <span class="nc">WindowType</span></code>

Which analysis window to taper a frame with before transforming it — the trade between how sharply you can separate two nearby frequencies and how much a strong one smears into its neighbours.

Constants: `RECTANGULAR`, `HANN`, `HAMMING`, `BLACKMAN`.

Symmetric (periodic=false) by default. |

The `periodic` distinction does not apply, so there is no such parameter. |

Symmetric unless `periodic` is true. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">fun</span> <span class="nf">hamming</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">n</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">periodic</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Boolean</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="kc">false</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">DoubleArray</span></code> | `0.54 - 0.46·cos(2πi/d)` — like `hann` but it does **not** reach zero at the ends, which is what buys its slightly better resolution and slightly worse far-field leakage. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">fun</span> <span class="nf">blackman</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">n</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">periodic</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Boolean</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="kc">false</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">DoubleArray</span></code> | The three-term `0.42 - 0.5·cos(w) + 0.08·cos(2w)` window: the strongest leakage suppression here, and the widest main lobe — about 1.5 times `hann`'s null-to-null width, so two frequencies Hann would just separate blur into one here. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">fun</span> <span class="nf">coherentGain</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">window</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">DoubleArray</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Double</span></code> | Coherent gain (mean) of a window — used to compensate amplitude when a window is applied. |

## stats.kt { #stats-kt }

Descriptive statistics, and the SVG/HTML renderings Field uses to put them in a box output.

`buildSummaryStats` reduces a sequence of doubles to a [`SummaryStats`](math.md#stats-kt-summarystats) — count, quartiles, IQR,
MAD, variance, skewness, excess kurtosis — dropping and counting non-finite values as it goes.
`buildHistogram` picks a bin width as the smallest of the Freedman–Diaconis, Scott and Sturges
estimates, clamped to at most 2000 bins. [`SummaryStatsBuffer`](math.md#stats-kt-summarystatsbuffer) wraps both behind a synchronized,
capped sliding window you can `add` to sample by sample; there are parallel
[`Vec2SummaryStats`](math.md#stats-kt-vec2summarystats) / [`Vec3SummaryStats`](math.md#stats-kt-vec3summarystats) / [`Vec4SummaryStats`](math.md#stats-kt-vec4summarystats) forms that carry per-component
stats, vector length and the pairwise component correlations, each with their own buffer.

The rendering half — `histogramToSvg`, `seriesPlotToSvg` and `summaryStatsBoxToHtml` — builds
SVG and HTML by string interpolation, with no drawing library involved, and defaults to
Field's cyan-on-black look through a long list of colour and padding parameters. Pass the
previous [`SummaryStats`](math.md#stats-kt-summarystats) and changed numbers are tinted by the sign and relative size of the
change. `seriesPlotToSvg` envelope-downsamples to `maxSeriesPoints` (500) before drawing.

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/stdlib/stats.kt`

**Used in:** [Which of these signals actually depend on each other?](../statistics_examples.md)

## timeseries.kt { #timeseries-kt }

Streaming, time-domain filters over `Float` signals — the sample-at-a-time counterpart to the
frequency-domain code in `spectral.kt`.

Everything here implements the [`FloatFilter`](math.md#timeseries-kt-floatfilter) fun interface (one `Float` in, one `Float` out)
and composes with `then`, so a chain reads as
`DCBlocker() then EMAFilter(0.1f) then NoiseGate(0.05f)`. Three families share that interface:
smoothers and classic filters ([`EMAFilter`](math.md#timeseries-kt-emafilter), [`AlphaBetaFilter`](math.md#timeseries-kt-alphabetafilter), [`OneEuroFilter`](math.md#timeseries-kt-oneeurofilter), [`BiquadFilter`](math.md#timeseries-kt-biquadfilter)
with its `LowPassFilter` / `HighPassFilter` / `BandPassFilter` / `BandRejectFilter`
constructors); rolling distribution fits — exponential, gamma, beta and Rayleigh — each
paired with a `Normalizer` mapping the fitted CDF into a target range and an `EventDetector`
firing on tail probability ([`ZScoreEventDetector`](math.md#timeseries-kt-zscoreeventdetector) instead thresholds on standard deviations
from a rolling mean); and utility stages such as [`MedianFilter`](math.md#timeseries-kt-medianfilter), [`SchmittTrigger`](math.md#timeseries-kt-schmitttrigger), [`AGC`](math.md#timeseries-kt-agc),
[`PIDController`](math.md#timeseries-kt-pidcontroller), [`LeakyIntegrator`](math.md#timeseries-kt-leakyintegrator) and [`DynamicRangeCompressor`](math.md#timeseries-kt-dynamicrangecompressor).

Pure Kotlin with no external dependency: the log-gamma, regularized incomplete gamma and
regularized incomplete beta functions the distribution fits need are implemented privately at
the top of this file. Filters are stateful objects, so use one instance per signal, and the
window-based ones allocate their ring buffer up front from `windowSize`.

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/stdlib/timeseries.kt`

**Used in:** [Timeseries examples](../timeseries_examples.md), [Spectral examples](../spectral_examples.md)

### Top-level functions { #timeseries-kt-functions }

| Declaration | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">fun</span> <span class="nf">LowPassFilter</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">frequency</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">sampleRate</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">q</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mf">0.707f</span><span class="p">)</span></code> | A [`BiquadFilter`](math.md#timeseries-kt-biquadfilter) that passes what is below `frequency` (Hz) and rolls off above it at 12 dB/octave. `sampleRate` is the rate of the stream in Hz — both are needed, because only their ratio means anything. `q` defaults to the maximally-flat 0.707; raise it for a resonant bump at the corner. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">fun</span> <span class="nf">HighPassFilter</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">frequency</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">sampleRate</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">q</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mf">0.707f</span><span class="p">)</span></code> | A [`BiquadFilter`](math.md#timeseries-kt-biquadfilter) that passes what is above `frequency` (Hz) and rolls off below it at 12 dB/octave — the steeper, better-specified alternative to `DCBlocker` once you know the corner you actually want. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">fun</span> <span class="nf">BandPassFilter</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">frequency</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">sampleRate</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">q</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mf">0.707f</span><span class="p">)</span></code> | A [`BiquadFilter`](math.md#timeseries-kt-biquadfilter) that keeps a band around `frequency` (Hz) and rejects both sides of it. With a single biquad, `q` *is* the bandwidth (`bandwidth ≈ frequency / q`), so the 0.707 default is very wide indeed — push it to 4 or 8 for something that isolates a component. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">fun</span> <span class="nf">BandRejectFilter</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">frequency</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">sampleRate</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">q</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mf">0.707f</span><span class="p">)</span></code> | A [`BiquadFilter`](math.md#timeseries-kt-biquadfilter) that notches out `frequency` (Hz) and passes everything else — mains hum, a rig's resonance, one offending tone. Higher `q` gives a narrower notch; this is `BiquadType.NOTCH` under a friendlier name. |

### FloatFilter { #timeseries-kt-floatfilter }

<code class="highlight"><span class="k">fun</span> <span class="k">interface</span> <span class="nc">FloatFilter</span></code>

One `Float` in, one `Float` out — the shape every filter in this file takes, and the reason they chain. A filter is a stateful object called once per sample, in arrival order: it is not a pure function, and calling it is what advances its state, so never call one twice on the same sample just to read a number back out of it.

| Declaration | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">operator</span> <span class="k">fun</span> <span class="nf">invoke</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">value</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span></code> | Push one sample through and take this stage's output for it, advancing the filter's state. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">infix</span> <span class="k">fun</span> <span class="nf">then</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">next</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">FloatFilter</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">FloatFilter</span></code> | Series composition, left to right: `a then b` feeds `a`'s output into `b`, so `DCBlocker() then EMAFilter(0.1f)` takes the offset out first and smooths what is left. |

### EMAFilter { #timeseries-kt-emafilter }

<code class="highlight"><span class="k">class</span> <span class="nf">EMAFilter</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">alpha</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span><span class="p">)</span> <span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">FloatFilter</span></code>

Exponential moving average — the cheapest useful smoother, `out = alpha * in + (1 - alpha) * out`. One multiply-add and one field of state, which is why it is so often the first thing in a chain.

| Declaration | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">override</span> <span class="k">fun</span> <span class="nf">invoke</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">value</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span></code> | The smoothed value for `value` — on the very first call, `value` itself. |

### AlphaBetaFilter { #timeseries-kt-alphabetafilter }

<code class="highlight"><span class="k">class</span> <span class="nf">AlphaBetaFilter</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">alpha</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">beta</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">dt</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mi">1f</span><span class="p">)</span> <span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">FloatFilter</span></code>

A constant-velocity tracker with fixed gains — a Kalman filter's structure without its bookkeeping. It carries a position *and* a velocity, predicts one step ahead, then corrects both from the residual, so unlike [`EMAFilter`](math.md#timeseries-kt-emafilter) it keeps up with a steadily moving signal instead of trailing behind it.

| Declaration | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">override</span> <span class="k">fun</span> <span class="nf">invoke</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">value</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span></code> | The corrected position estimate for `value`. The internal velocity is updated too, but is not exposed. |

### OneEuroFilter { #timeseries-kt-oneeurofilter }

<code class="highlight"><span class="k">class</span> <span class="nf">OneEuroFilter</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">minCutoff</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mf">1.0f</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">beta</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mf">0.0f</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">dCutoff</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mf">1.0f</span><span class="p">)</span> <span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">FloatFilter</span></code>

The 1€ filter (Casiez, Roussel & Vogel): a low-pass whose cutoff rises with the signal's own speed, so a slow-moving hand gets smoothed hard while a fast gesture is barely delayed. The usual pick for pointer, touch or tracker input, where lag is more objectionable than jitter.

| Declaration | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">minCutoff</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span></code> | Cutoff (Hz) used when the signal is standing still — lower is smoother and laggier. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">beta</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span></code> | How strongly measured speed raises the cutoff: `cutoff = minCutoff + beta * \|speed\|`. At 0 the adaptation is off and this is an ordinary one-pole low-pass at `minCutoff`. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">dCutoff</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span></code> | Cutoff (Hz) of the low-pass applied to the speed estimate itself. Raise it if the adaptation feels sluggish, lower it if noise in the speed makes the cutoff jitter. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">override</span> <span class="k">fun</span> <span class="nf">invoke</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">value</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span></code> | The filtered sample. Reads the clock, so the amount of smoothing depends on *when* you call this, not only on what you pass in. |

### BiquadType { #timeseries-kt-biquadtype }

<code class="highlight"><span class="k">enum</span> <span class="k">class</span> <span class="nc">BiquadType</span></code>

Which of the RBJ audio-EQ-cookbook shapes a [`BiquadFilter`](math.md#timeseries-kt-biquadfilter) realises. `LOWPASS`, `HIGHPASS`, `BANDPASS` and `NOTCH` are determined entirely by frequency and Q; `PEAK`, `LOWSHELF` and `HIGHSHELF` are the only three that read `gainDb` — the others accept it and ignore it.

Constants: `LOWPASS`, `HIGHPASS`, `BANDPASS`, `NOTCH`, `PEAK`, `LOWSHELF`, `HIGHSHELF`.

### BiquadFilter { #timeseries-kt-biquadfilter }

<code class="highlight"><span class="k">class</span> <span class="nf">BiquadFilter</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">type</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">BiquadType</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">frequency</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">sampleRate</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">q</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mf">0.707f</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">gainDb</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mi">0f</span><span class="p">)</span> <span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">FloatFilter</span></code>

A second-order IIR section — two poles, two zeros — run as a direct-form I recursion with coefficients from the RBJ audio-EQ cookbook. This is the machinery behind `LowPassFilter`, `HighPassFilter`, `BandPassFilter` and `BandRejectFilter`, and what to reach for when you want a filter with an actual corner frequency rather than a vague smoothing coefficient.

| Declaration | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">type</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">BiquadType</span></code> | The response shape. Fixed at construction — build a new filter to change it. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">frequency</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span></code> | Corner (or centre) frequency in Hz. Call `calculateCoefficients` after changing it. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">sampleRate</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span></code> | The rate in Hz of the stream you will push through: the reference `frequency` is measured against, and not something the filter can discover for itself. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">q</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span></code> | Resonance. `0.707` is maximally flat (Butterworth); higher peaks at the corner and rings, and for `BiquadType.BANDPASS` / `BiquadType.NOTCH` higher also means a narrower band. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">gainDb</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span></code> | Boost (positive) or cut (negative) in dB — read only by `BiquadType.PEAK`, `BiquadType.LOWSHELF` and `BiquadType.HIGHSHELF`, and silently ignored by the other four. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">fun</span> <span class="nf">calculateCoefficients</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="p">)</span></code> | Re-derive the five coefficients from the current `type`, `frequency`, `sampleRate`, `q` and `gainDb`. Run once at construction; run it again yourself after mutating any of those, because nothing else will. It deliberately leaves the delay line alone, so a mid-stream retune stays continuous in the signal but can step the output audibly. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">override</span> <span class="k">fun</span> <span class="nf">invoke</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">value</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span></code> | One step of `y = b0·x + b1·x₋₁ + b2·x₋₂ − a1·y₋₁ − a2·y₋₂`, shifting the two input and two output delays along afterwards. |

### RollingStats { #timeseries-kt-rollingstats }

<code class="highlight"><span class="k">class</span> <span class="nf">RollingStats</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">windowSize</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span><span class="p">)</span> <span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">FloatFilter</span></code>

A tap rather than a filter: every sample passes through unchanged, and the window's `mean`, `variance`, `stdDev` and the current sample's `zScore` are left behind for you to read. Drop it anywhere in a `then` chain to find out what the signal is doing at that point without disturbing it.

| Declaration | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">mean</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span></code> | Arithmetic mean of the window, the sample just pushed included. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">variance</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span></code> | Sample (n−1) variance of the window; 0 until a second sample has arrived. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">stdDev</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span></code> | Square root of `variance`. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">zScore</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span></code> | How many standard deviations the sample just pushed sits from `mean` — signed, and 0 whenever `stdDev` is 0. Note the sample is itself in the window it is being compared against. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">override</span> <span class="k">fun</span> <span class="nf">invoke</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">value</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span></code> | Records `value` into the window, refreshes all four statistics, and hands `value` straight back. |

### RollingExponentialStats { #timeseries-kt-rollingexponentialstats }

<code class="highlight"><span class="k">class</span> <span class="nf">RollingExponentialStats</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">windowSize</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">epsilon</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="nc">DISTRIBUTION&#95;EPSILON</span><span class="p">)</span> <span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">FloatFilter</span></code>

Fits an exponential distribution to the last `windowSize` samples by moment matching (`lambda = 1 / mean`) and reports where the newest sample falls within it. A tap: the sample passes through unchanged.

| Declaration | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">windowSize</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span></code> | How many samples the fit sees. Must be `>= 2`; the ring buffer is allocated up front. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">epsilon</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span></code> | Degeneracy floor. While the fitted mean or rate is at or below this the fit is abandoned rather than dividing by something near zero. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">mean</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span></code> | Mean of the window after negative clamping — the only statistic an exponential fit needs. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">lambda</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span></code> | Fitted rate `1 / mean`, or 0 while the window mean is at or below `epsilon`. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">variance</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span></code> | Variance *of the fitted distribution*, `1 / lambda²` — not the sample variance of the window. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">stdDev</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span></code> | Square root of `variance`, so also `1 / lambda`. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">cdf</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span></code> | `P(X <= x)` under the fit for the sample just pushed, in `0..1`. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">tailProbability</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span></code> | `P(X >= x) = 1 - cdf` for the sample just pushed: small means a surprisingly large sample. Sits at 1 during the degenerate case, so a silent signal reports nothing as unusual. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">clippedNegativeCount</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Long</span></code> | How many negative samples have been clamped to zero so far. Anything but 0 means the exponential is the wrong model for this signal — take `abs()` first, or use [`RollingBetaStats`](math.md#timeseries-kt-rollingbetastats). |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">override</span> <span class="k">fun</span> <span class="nf">invoke</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">value</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span></code> | Clamps `value` to `>= 0`, refits the window, updates `cdf` and `tailProbability` — and returns the original `value`, clamping and all left behind in the fit. |

### ExponentialNormalizer { #timeseries-kt-exponentialnormalizer }

<code class="highlight"><span class="k">class</span> <span class="nf">ExponentialNormalizer</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">windowSize</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">targetMin</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mi">0f</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">targetMax</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mi">1f</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">epsilon</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="nc">DISTRIBUTION&#95;EPSILON</span><span class="p">)</span> <span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">FloatFilter</span></code>

Rescales a non-negative stream by *rank* rather than by magnitude: each sample's fitted exponential CDF, mapped onto `targetMin..targetMax`. What you want when an unbounded intensity has to drive something that expects a bounded control value, and "big for this signal lately" matters more than the units.

| Declaration | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">targetMin</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span></code> | The value a CDF of 0 maps to. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">targetMax</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span></code> | The value a CDF of 1 maps to. May be set below `targetMin` to invert the mapping. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">stats</span></code> | The fit doing the work — read `stats.lambda`, `stats.tailProbability` or `stats.clippedNegativeCount` to see what the normaliser is basing its answer on. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">override</span> <span class="k">fun</span> <span class="nf">invoke</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">value</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span></code> | Pushes `value` through the fit and returns its CDF mapped into `targetMin..targetMax`. |

### ExponentialEventDetector { #timeseries-kt-exponentialeventdetector }

<code class="highlight"><span class="k">class</span> <span class="nf">ExponentialEventDetector</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">windowSize</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">tailProbabilityThreshold</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mf">0.01f</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">influence</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mi">0f</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">epsilon</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="nc">DISTRIBUTION&#95;EPSILON</span><span class="p">)</span> <span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">FloatFilter</span></code>

Fires when a sample is improbably large for the exponential distribution the preceding window fits — an onset / spike detector for non-negative streams, in the same family as [`ZScoreEventDetector`](math.md#timeseries-kt-zscoreeventdetector) but thresholding tail probability instead of standard deviations.

| Declaration | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">windowSize</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span></code> | Samples of history behind the fit. Must be `>= 2`, and nothing can fire until this many have arrived. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">tailProbabilityThreshold</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span></code> | Fire when the sample's upper-tail probability falls to this or below — at 0.01, "in the top 1% of the fitted distribution". Clamped into `0..1` on use. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">influence</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span></code> | How much of an event's own sample is written into the window, `0..1` (clamped): 0 keeps events out of the fit entirely, 1 lets them recalibrate it so a sustained shift stops being news. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">epsilon</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span></code> | Degeneracy floor — while the window mean is at or below this, no events are reported at all. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">isEvent</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Boolean</span></code> | Whether the most recent sample fired — the same news as a nonzero return from `invoke`. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">tailProbability</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span></code> | Upper-tail probability of the most recent sample; 1 during warm-up and while the fit is degenerate. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">lambda</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span></code> | Fitted exponential rate `1 / mean` over the window, or 0 while degenerate. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">clippedNegativeCount</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Long</span></code> | How many negative samples have been clamped to zero — anything but 0 means the wrong model for this signal. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">override</span> <span class="k">fun</span> <span class="nf">invoke</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">value</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span></code> | `1f` if `value` is an event, `0f` otherwise — including for every sample of the warm-up. |

### RollingGammaStats { #timeseries-kt-rollinggammastats }

<code class="highlight"><span class="k">class</span> <span class="nf">RollingGammaStats</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">windowSize</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">epsilon</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="nc">DISTRIBUTION&#95;EPSILON</span><span class="p">)</span> <span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">FloatFilter</span></code>

Fits a gamma distribution to the last `windowSize` samples by matching mean and variance (`shape = mean²/variance`, `scale = variance/mean`) and reports where the newest sample falls within it. A tap: the sample passes through unchanged.

| Declaration | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">windowSize</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span></code> | How many samples the fit sees. Must be `>= 2`; the ring buffer is allocated up front. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">epsilon</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span></code> | Degeneracy floor for the window's mean and variance, and the lower bound clamped onto the fitted shape and scale. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">mean</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span></code> | Arithmetic mean of the window after negative clamping — half of the moment-matching fit. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">variance</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span></code> | Sample (n−1) variance of the window — a genuine sample statistic here, and the other half of the fit. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">stdDev</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span></code> | Square root of `variance`. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">shape</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span></code> | Fitted gamma shape `mean²/variance` (the `k` parameter): 1 would be an exponential, larger is more symmetric. 0 while the fit is degenerate. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">scale</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span></code> | Fitted gamma scale `variance/mean` (the `θ` parameter), in the units of your signal. 0 while degenerate. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">cdf</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span></code> | `P(X <= x)` under the fit for the sample just pushed, in `0..1`. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">tailProbability</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span></code> | `1 - cdf`: the share of the fitted distribution lying above the current sample. Small means surprisingly large. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">clippedNegativeCount</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Long</span></code> | How many negative samples have been clamped to zero — anything but 0 means a gamma is the wrong model here. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">override</span> <span class="k">fun</span> <span class="nf">invoke</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">value</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span></code> | Clamps `value` to `>= 0`, re-matches shape and scale over the window, updates `cdf` and `tailProbability`, and returns the original `value` untouched. |

### GammaNormalizer { #timeseries-kt-gammanormalizer }

<code class="highlight"><span class="k">class</span> <span class="nf">GammaNormalizer</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">windowSize</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">targetMin</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mi">0f</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">targetMax</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mi">1f</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">epsilon</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="nc">DISTRIBUTION&#95;EPSILON</span><span class="p">)</span> <span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">FloatFilter</span></code>

Rescales a non-negative, skewed stream onto `targetMin..targetMax` by its fitted gamma CDF — the two-parameter sibling of [`ExponentialNormalizer`](math.md#timeseries-kt-exponentialnormalizer), and the better pick whenever the signal's bulk sits somewhere away from zero rather than hugging it.

| Declaration | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">targetMin</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span></code> | The value a CDF of 0 maps to. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">targetMax</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span></code> | The value a CDF of 1 maps to. May be set below `targetMin` to invert the mapping. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">stats</span></code> | The fit doing the work — read `stats.shape` and `stats.scale` to see what distribution the answers came from. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">override</span> <span class="k">fun</span> <span class="nf">invoke</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">value</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span></code> | Pushes `value` through the fit and returns its CDF mapped into `targetMin..targetMax`. |

### GammaEventDetector { #timeseries-kt-gammaeventdetector }

<code class="highlight"><span class="k">class</span> <span class="nf">GammaEventDetector</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">windowSize</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">tailProbabilityThreshold</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mf">0.01f</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">influence</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mi">0f</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">epsilon</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="nc">DISTRIBUTION&#95;EPSILON</span><span class="p">)</span> <span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">FloatFilter</span></code>

Fires when a sample lands in the upper tail of the gamma distribution the preceding window fits. The general-purpose distribution-aware onset detector in this file: it copes with the skewed, non-negative streams — magnitudes, energies, `abs()` of a motion signal — where a z-score's assumption of symmetry makes it over-fire on the low side. This is the detector the published `timeseries_examples` page reaches for.

| Declaration | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">windowSize</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span></code> | Samples of history behind the fit. Must be `>= 2`, and nothing fires until this many have arrived. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">tailProbabilityThreshold</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span></code> | Fire when the sample's upper-tail probability falls to this or below — at 0.01, "in the top 1% of the fitted distribution". Clamped into `0..1` on use. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">influence</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span></code> | How much of an event's own sample enters the window, `0..1` (clamped): 0 keeps events out of the fit, 1 lets them recalibrate it. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">epsilon</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span></code> | Degeneracy floor for the window's mean and variance — below it, no events are reported. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">isEvent</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Boolean</span></code> | Whether the most recent sample fired. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">cdf</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span></code> | `P(X <= x)` of the most recent sample under the fit; 0 during warm-up and while degenerate. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">tailProbability</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span></code> | `1 - cdf` for the most recent sample — the quantity actually compared with `tailProbabilityThreshold`. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">shape</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span></code> | Fitted gamma shape over the window, or 0 while the fit is degenerate. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">scale</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span></code> | Fitted gamma scale over the window, in the units of your signal, or 0 while degenerate. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">clippedNegativeCount</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Long</span></code> | How many negative samples have been clamped to zero — anything but 0 means the wrong model for this signal. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">override</span> <span class="k">fun</span> <span class="nf">invoke</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">value</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span></code> | `1f` if `value` is an event, `0f` otherwise — including for every sample of the warm-up. |

### RollingBetaStats { #timeseries-kt-rollingbetastats }

<code class="highlight"><span class="k">class</span> <span class="nf">RollingBetaStats</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">windowSize</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">supportMin</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mi">0f</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">supportMax</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mi">1f</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">epsilon</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mi">1e</span><span class="p">-</span><span class="mi">4f</span><span class="p">)</span> <span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">FloatFilter</span></code>

Fits a beta distribution to the last `windowSize` samples by moment matching and reports where the newest one falls within it. A tap: the sample passes through unchanged.

| Declaration | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">windowSize</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span></code> | How many samples the fit sees. Must be `>= 2`; the ring buffer is allocated up front. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">supportMin</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span></code> | Bottom of your signal's assumed range; anything below maps to 0 and counts as clipped. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">supportMax</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span></code> | Top of your signal's assumed range; anything above maps to 1 and counts as clipped. Must be strictly greater than `supportMin` at construction. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">epsilon</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span></code> | How far inside the open interval `(0, 1)` stored samples are held, and the degeneracy floor for the moment fit. Defaults to 1e-4, deliberately looser than the other fits in this file. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">mean</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span></code> | Mean of the window in *normalised* `0..1` units, not in the units of your signal. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">variance</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span></code> | Sample (n−1) variance of the window, also in normalised units. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">stdDev</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span></code> | Square root of `variance`. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">alpha</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span></code> | Fitted beta `α`, the shape pulling mass toward 1; 0 when the fit fell back to min/max normalisation. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">beta</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span></code> | Fitted beta `β`, the shape pulling mass toward 0; 0 when the fit fell back to min/max normalisation. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">cdf</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span></code> | `P(X <= x)` under the fit for the sample just pushed, in `0..1` — or, when the fit is degenerate, simply that sample's normalised position within the support. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">tailProbabilityLow</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span></code> | Lower-tail probability of the current sample; equal to `cdf`. Small means unusually low for this window. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">tailProbabilityHigh</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span></code> | Upper-tail probability of the current sample, `1 - cdf`. Small means unusually high. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">clippedToSupportCount</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Long</span></code> | How many samples have fallen outside `supportMin..supportMax` and been clipped into it. A count that keeps climbing means the support is wrong. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">normalizedValue</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span></code> | The sample just pushed, mapped onto `0..1` across the support — clipped there but *before* the epsilon nudge, so unlike the value stored in the window this one can be exactly 0 or 1. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">override</span> <span class="k">fun</span> <span class="nf">invoke</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">value</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span></code> | Normalises `value` into the support, refits the window, updates the CDF and both tails, and returns the original `value` unchanged. |

### BetaNormalizer { #timeseries-kt-betanormalizer }

<code class="highlight"><span class="k">class</span> <span class="nf">BetaNormalizer</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">windowSize</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">targetMin</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mi">0f</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">targetMax</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mi">1f</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">supportMin</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mi">0f</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">supportMax</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mi">1f</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">epsilon</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mi">1e</span><span class="p">-</span><span class="mi">4f</span><span class="p">)</span> <span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">FloatFilter</span></code>

Rescales a bounded stream onto `targetMin..targetMax` by its fitted beta CDF — histogram equalisation with a two-parameter distribution standing in for the histogram. Where [`RollingNormalizer`](math.md#timeseries-kt-rollingnormalizer) merely stretches the window's extremes apart, this spreads samples out according to how they are actually distributed, so a signal that spends its life bunched in one corner of its range comes out using the whole target range.

| Declaration | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">targetMin</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span></code> | The value a CDF of 0 maps to. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">targetMax</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span></code> | The value a CDF of 1 maps to. May be set below `targetMin` to invert the mapping. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">stats</span></code> | The fit doing the work. Also where the support lives after construction — and where `clippedToSupportCount` will tell you the support is wrong. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">override</span> <span class="k">fun</span> <span class="nf">invoke</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">value</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span></code> | Pushes `value` through the fit and returns its CDF mapped into `targetMin..targetMax`. |

### BetaEventDetector { #timeseries-kt-betaeventdetector }

<code class="highlight"><span class="k">class</span> <span class="nf">BetaEventDetector</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">windowSize</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">supportMin</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mi">0f</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">supportMax</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mi">1f</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">lowerTailThreshold</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mf">0.01f</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">upperTailThreshold</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mf">0.01f</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">influence</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mi">0f</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">epsilon</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mi">1e</span><span class="p">-</span><span class="mi">4f</span><span class="p">)</span> <span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">FloatFilter</span></code>

A two-sided event detector for a bounded stream: it fires both when a sample is improbably high for the window's fitted beta and when it is improbably low, and the sign of the output says which. `-1f` for a lower-tail event, `+1f` for an upper-tail one, `0f` for nothing — including for the whole `windowSize`-sample warm-up.

| Declaration | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">windowSize</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span></code> | Samples of history behind the fit. Must be `>= 2`, and nothing fires until this many have arrived. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">supportMin</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span></code> | Bottom of your signal's assumed range; anything below is clipped to it and counted. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">supportMax</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span></code> | Top of your signal's assumed range; must be strictly greater than `supportMin` at construction. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">lowerTailThreshold</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span></code> | Fire low when the CDF falls to this or below — at 0.01, "in the bottom 1% of the fit". Clamped into `0..1`; set above 0.5 and nearly everything becomes an event. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">upperTailThreshold</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span></code> | Fire high when `1 - cdf` falls to this or below — the top 1% at 0.01. Clamped into `0..1`. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">influence</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span></code> | How much of an event's own sample enters the window, `0..1` (clamped): 0 keeps events out of the fit, 1 lets a sustained shift recalibrate it. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">epsilon</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span></code> | Boundary nudge for stored samples and degeneracy floor for the moment fit; 1e-4 by default. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">isEvent</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Boolean</span></code> | Whether the most recent sample fired at either end. It does not say which end — the sign of `invoke`'s return does. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">cdf</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span></code> | CDF of the most recent sample under the fit, or its normalised position when degenerate; parked at 0.5 during warm-up. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">alpha</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span></code> | Fitted beta `α` over the window; 0 when the fit fell back to plain normalisation. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">beta</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span></code> | Fitted beta `β` over the window; 0 when the fit fell back to plain normalisation. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">clippedToSupportCount</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Long</span></code> | How many samples have been clipped into `supportMin..supportMax` — a climbing count means the support is wrong. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">override</span> <span class="k">fun</span> <span class="nf">invoke</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">value</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span></code> | `-1f` for a lower-tail event, `+1f` for an upper-tail one, `0f` for neither and for the whole warm-up. If both thresholds somehow fire at once, the lower tail wins. |

### RollingRayleighStats { #timeseries-kt-rollingrayleighstats }

<code class="highlight"><span class="k">class</span> <span class="nf">RollingRayleighStats</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">windowSize</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">epsilon</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="nc">DISTRIBUTION&#95;EPSILON</span><span class="p">)</span> <span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">FloatFilter</span></code>

Fits a Rayleigh distribution to the last `windowSize` samples and reports where the newest one falls within it. A tap: the sample passes through unchanged.

| Declaration | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">windowSize</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span></code> | How many samples the fit sees. Must be `>= 2`; the ring buffer is allocated up front. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">epsilon</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span></code> | Degeneracy floor on the window's second moment and on `sigma` — below it, nothing is reported. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">sigma</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span></code> | Fitted Rayleigh scale, `sqrt(mean(x²) / 2)`; 0 while the window's second moment is at or below `epsilon`. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">mean</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span></code> | Mean *of the fitted distribution*, `sigma * sqrt(π/2)` — derived from `sigma`, not averaged from the window. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">variance</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span></code> | Variance of the fitted distribution, `((4 - π)/2) * sigma²`. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">stdDev</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span></code> | Square root of `variance`. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">cdf</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span></code> | `P(X <= x) = 1 - exp(-x² / 2sigma²)` for the sample just pushed. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">tailProbability</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span></code> | `1 - cdf`: the share of the fitted distribution above the current sample. Small means a surprisingly large magnitude. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">clippedNegativeCount</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Long</span></code> | How many negative samples have been clamped to zero. A magnitude should never be negative, so anything but 0 means the wrong signal is arriving here. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">override</span> <span class="k">fun</span> <span class="nf">invoke</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">value</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span></code> | Clamps `value` to `>= 0`, re-estimates `sigma` from the window's second moment, updates the fitted moments and the CDF, and returns the original `value` unchanged. |

### RayleighNormalizer { #timeseries-kt-rayleighnormalizer }

<code class="highlight"><span class="k">class</span> <span class="nf">RayleighNormalizer</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">windowSize</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">targetMin</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mi">0f</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">targetMax</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mi">1f</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">epsilon</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="nc">DISTRIBUTION&#95;EPSILON</span><span class="p">)</span> <span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">FloatFilter</span></code>

Rescales a stream of magnitudes onto `targetMin..targetMax` by its fitted Rayleigh CDF. The one to use when the numbers arriving are lengths of 2-D vectors — cursor speed, optical-flow magnitude, gradient strength — because a single-parameter fit adapts on far less history than [`GammaNormalizer`](math.md#timeseries-kt-gammanormalizer) needs.

| Declaration | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">targetMin</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span></code> | The value a CDF of 0 maps to. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">targetMax</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span></code> | The value a CDF of 1 maps to. May be set below `targetMin` to invert the mapping. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">stats</span></code> | The fit doing the work — `stats.sigma` is the single number the whole mapping rests on. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">override</span> <span class="k">fun</span> <span class="nf">invoke</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">value</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span></code> | Pushes `value` through the fit and returns its CDF mapped into `targetMin..targetMax`. |

### RayleighEventDetector { #timeseries-kt-rayleigheventdetector }

<code class="highlight"><span class="k">class</span> <span class="nf">RayleighEventDetector</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">windowSize</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">tailProbabilityThreshold</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mf">0.01f</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">influence</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mi">0f</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">epsilon</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="nc">DISTRIBUTION&#95;EPSILON</span><span class="p">)</span> <span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">FloatFilter</span></code>

Fires when a magnitude is improbably large for the Rayleigh distribution the preceding window fits. The detector to pair with a speed or vector-length signal: a sudden lunge, a flick, a burst of optical flow.

| Declaration | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">windowSize</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span></code> | Samples of history behind the fit. Must be `>= 2`, and nothing fires until this many have arrived. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">tailProbabilityThreshold</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span></code> | Fire when the sample's upper-tail probability falls to this or below — at 0.01, "in the top 1% of the fitted distribution". Clamped into `0..1` on use. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">influence</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span></code> | How much of an event's own sample enters the window, `0..1` (clamped): 0 keeps events out of the fit, 1 lets them recalibrate it. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">epsilon</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span></code> | Degeneracy floor on the window's second moment and on `sigma` — below it, no events are reported. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">isEvent</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Boolean</span></code> | Whether the most recent sample fired. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">sigma</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span></code> | Fitted Rayleigh scale over the window, `sqrt(mean(x²) / 2)`, or 0 while degenerate. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">cdf</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span></code> | `P(X <= x)` of the most recent sample under the fit; 0 during warm-up and while degenerate. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">tailProbability</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span></code> | `1 - cdf` for the most recent sample — the quantity compared with `tailProbabilityThreshold`. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">clippedNegativeCount</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Long</span></code> | How many negative samples have been clamped to zero; a magnitude should never be negative. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">override</span> <span class="k">fun</span> <span class="nf">invoke</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">value</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span></code> | `1f` if `value` is an event, `0f` otherwise — including for every sample of the warm-up. |

### ZScoreEventDetector { #timeseries-kt-zscoreeventdetector }

<code class="highlight"><span class="k">class</span> <span class="nf">ZScoreEventDetector</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">windowSize</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">threshold</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">influence</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span><span class="p">)</span> <span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">FloatFilter</span></code>

The classic smoothed z-score peak detector: it fires when the newest sample sits more than `threshold` standard deviations from the mean of the window, and its output carries the direction — `+1f` above, `-1f` below, `0f` for no event and throughout the warm-up.

| Declaration | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">windowSize</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span></code> | Samples of history behind the mean and standard deviation; nothing fires until this many have arrived. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">threshold</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span></code> | How many standard deviations from the window mean counts as an event — 3 to 4 is a conventional starting point. The test is strict and on `\|z\|`, so it fires in both directions. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">influence</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span></code> | How much of an event's own sample enters the window, nominally `0..1` but **not** clamped: 0 substitutes the previous sample, so a sustained level shift keeps being reported forever, while 1 lets the detector adapt to it and fall silent. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">isEvent</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Boolean</span></code> | Whether the most recent sample fired, in either direction. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">override</span> <span class="k">fun</span> <span class="nf">invoke</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">value</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span></code> | `+1f` or `-1f` for an event above or below the window, `0f` for none — and `0f` for the first `windowSize` samples while the window fills, and whenever the window is perfectly flat. |

### AdaptiveCompander { #timeseries-kt-adaptivecompander }

<code class="highlight"><span class="k">class</span> <span class="nf">AdaptiveCompander</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">attack</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mf">0.01f</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">release</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mf">0.1f</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">threshold</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mf">0.5f</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">ratio</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mf">2.0f</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">isCompressor</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Boolean</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="kc">true</span><span class="p">)</span> <span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">FloatFilter</span></code>

An envelope follower plus a static gain curve: it either squashes the loud parts toward `threshold` (compressor) or pushes the quiet parts further down (expander), depending on `isCompressor`. Everything is in linear units, which makes this the plain, cheap sibling of [`DynamicRangeCompressor`](math.md#timeseries-kt-dynamicrangecompressor) — that one does the same job in dB, with a soft knee and real attack and release times.

| Declaration | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">attack</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span></code> | Per-sample coefficient (`0..1`) used while the envelope is *rising*; larger reacts faster to a growing signal. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">release</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span></code> | Per-sample coefficient (`0..1`) used while the envelope is *falling*; larger lets the gain recover faster after a peak. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">threshold</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span></code> | The linear amplitude where the curve bends — above it for a compressor, below it for an expander. Not dB. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">ratio</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span></code> | How hard the curve bends: as a compressor the excess above `threshold` is divided by this; as an expander the shortfall below it is multiplied by it. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">isCompressor</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Boolean</span></code> | `true` compresses (pull the loud parts in), `false` expands (push the quiet parts down). Switchable mid-stream. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">override</span> <span class="k">fun</span> <span class="nf">invoke</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">value</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span></code> | Updates the envelope from `abs(value)` and returns `value` scaled by the gain the curve asks for at that envelope. |

### AGC { #timeseries-kt-agc }

<code class="highlight"><span class="k">class</span> <span class="nf">AGC</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">targetLevel</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mf">1.0f</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">attack</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mf">0.01f</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">release</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mf">0.001f</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">maxGain</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mf">10.0f</span><span class="p">)</span> <span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">FloatFilter</span></code>

Automatic gain control: follows the signal's envelope and scales the signal so that envelope sits at `targetLevel`.
