Reach for it when you care about the *shape* of a signal whose absolute scale you cannot predict — a sensor whose range depends on how it was mounted, a control stream you want to hand to something expecting `0..1`.

| Declaration | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">targetLevel</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span></code> | The envelope level the gain chases, in the same linear units as your signal. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">attack</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span></code> | Per-sample coefficient (`0..1`) used when the envelope rises and when the gain must increase; larger is faster. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">release</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span></code> | Per-sample coefficient (`0..1`) used when the envelope falls and when the gain must decrease. The default is deliberately ten times slower than `attack`, so the gain backs off gently. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">maxGain</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span></code> | Ceiling on the multiplier, so a near-silent stretch cannot be amplified without limit. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">override</span> <span class="k">fun</span> <span class="nf">invoke</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">value</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span></code> | Updates the envelope and the smoothed gain, then returns `value` multiplied by that gain. |

### LeakyIntegrator { #timeseries-kt-leakyintegrator }

<code class="highlight"><span class="k">class</span> <span class="nf">LeakyIntegrator</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">leakRate</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mf">0.99f</span><span class="p">)</span> <span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">FloatFilter</span></code>

A running sum that forgets: `sum = sum * leakRate + value`. The signal-processing way to ask "how much has been going on lately" — feed it event flags or rectified magnitudes and it climbs with activity, then decays back down when things go quiet.

| Declaration | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">override</span> <span class="k">fun</span> <span class="nf">invoke</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">value</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span></code> | Leaks the accumulator once, adds `value`, and returns the new total. Starts from 0 and has no reset. |

### RollingNormalizer { #timeseries-kt-rollingnormalizer }

<code class="highlight"><span class="k">class</span> <span class="nf">RollingNormalizer</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">windowSize</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">targetMin</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="p">-</span><span class="mi">1f</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">targetMax</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mi">1f</span><span class="p">)</span> <span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">FloatFilter</span></code>

Stretches the last `windowSize` samples onto `targetMin..targetMax` using their own minimum and maximum — the simplest auto-ranging there is, and the one to use when you know nothing about the signal's distribution and just need something bounded. Note the default target is `-1..1`, not `0..1`.

| Declaration | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">override</span> <span class="k">fun</span> <span class="nf">invoke</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">value</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span></code> | Records `value`, then returns it rescaled from the window's current min..max onto `targetMin..targetMax` — or the midpoint of that range while the window is flat. |

### RollingOneDollarNormalizer { #timeseries-kt-rollingonedollarnormalizer }

<code class="highlight"><span class="k">class</span> <span class="nf">RollingOneDollarNormalizer</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">windowSize</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span><span class="p">)</span> <span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">FloatFilter</span></code>

Centres the stream on its window mean and divides by the largest absolute deviation in that window, so the output lands in `-1..1` with `±1` reached exactly by whichever sample is currently furthest from the mean. A symmetric, zero-centred alternative to [`RollingNormalizer`](math.md#timeseries-kt-rollingnormalizer): "which side of typical" stays meaningful, at the price of letting one outlier set the scale for a whole window.

| Declaration | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">override</span> <span class="k">fun</span> <span class="nf">invoke</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">value</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span></code> | Records `value` and returns its deviation from the window mean divided by the window's largest absolute deviation; 0 while the window is constant. |

### AdaptiveThresholder { #timeseries-kt-adaptivethresholder }

<code class="highlight"><span class="k">class</span> <span class="nf">AdaptiveThresholder</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">windowSize</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mi">100</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">stdDevMultiplier</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mf">2.0f</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">clamp</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Boolean</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="kc">false</span><span class="p">)</span> <span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">FloatFilter</span></code>

Despite the name this returns a continuous value, not a decision: the sample's distance from the window mean, measured in units of `stdDevMultiplier` standard deviations. A sample sitting exactly `stdDevMultiplier` sigma above the mean comes out as `+1`, and it is thresholding that downstream — or a [`SchmittTrigger`](math.md#timeseries-kt-schmitttrigger) — that turns it into a decision.

| Declaration | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">windowSize</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span></code> | Samples of history behind the mean and standard deviation. The buffer is allocated up front. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">stdDevMultiplier</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span></code> | How many standard deviations map to an output of 1. Larger is a gentler scale. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">clamp</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Boolean</span></code> | Coerce the output into `-1..1` instead of letting it run past the ends. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">override</span> <span class="k">fun</span> <span class="nf">invoke</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">value</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span></code> | Records `value` and returns its deviation from the window mean divided by `stdDev * stdDevMultiplier`, optionally clamped to `-1..1`. |

### DerivativeFilter { #timeseries-kt-derivativefilter }

<code class="highlight"><span class="k">class</span> <span class="nc">DerivativeFilter</span> <span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">FloatFilter</span></code>

First difference: this sample minus the previous one. The cheapest way to turn something position-shaped into something velocity-shaped, or to find the edges in a slow signal.

| Declaration | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">override</span> <span class="k">fun</span> <span class="nf">invoke</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">value</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span></code> | The change since the previous sample, or 0 on the first call. |

### IntegralFilter { #timeseries-kt-integralfilter }

<code class="highlight"><span class="k">class</span> <span class="nc">IntegralFilter</span> <span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">FloatFilter</span></code>

A plain running total of everything it has ever been given — for accumulating an event count, or for turning a velocity-shaped signal back into a position-shaped one.

| Declaration | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">override</span> <span class="k">fun</span> <span class="nf">invoke</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">value</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span></code> | Adds `value` to the total and returns the new total. |

### DCBlocker { #timeseries-kt-dcblocker }

<code class="highlight"><span class="k">class</span> <span class="nf">DCBlocker</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">r</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mf">0.995f</span><span class="p">)</span> <span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">FloatFilter</span></code>

Removes whatever constant offset a signal is riding on, without waiting for a window to fill: a one-pole, one-zero high-pass, `y = x - x₋₁ + r·y₋₁`, parked just above DC. The standard thing to put at the head of a chain when you care how a sensor is *changing* rather than where its zero happens to sit.

| Declaration | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">override</span> <span class="k">fun</span> <span class="nf">invoke</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">value</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span></code> | One step of `y = x - x₋₁ + r·y₋₁` — the input with its slow-moving offset taken out. |

### PeakDetector { #timeseries-kt-peakdetector }

<code class="highlight"><span class="k">class</span> <span class="nf">PeakDetector</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">decay</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mf">0.99f</span><span class="p">)</span> <span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">FloatFilter</span></code>

A peak-hold envelope: it jumps instantly to `abs(value)` whenever that exceeds the current peak, and otherwise decays toward zero by a factor of `decay` each sample. What you want for a level meter, a "how hard was that hit" reading, or the denominator of a hand-rolled normaliser.

| Declaration | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">override</span> <span class="k">fun</span> <span class="nf">invoke</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">value</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span></code> | The held peak after `value`: its magnitude if that is a new high, otherwise the previous peak decayed once — but never less than the magnitude in hand. |

### SchmittTrigger { #timeseries-kt-schmitttrigger }

<code class="highlight"><span class="k">class</span> <span class="nf">SchmittTrigger</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">lowThreshold</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">highThreshold</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span><span class="p">)</span> <span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">FloatFilter</span></code>

A comparator with hysteresis: it goes high once the input rises above `highThreshold` and only comes back down once the input falls below `lowThreshold`, so a signal loitering around a single threshold cannot chatter. Returns `1f` while high and `0f` while low.

| Declaration | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">override</span> <span class="k">fun</span> <span class="nf">invoke</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">value</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span></code> | `1f` while latched high and `0f` while low, after letting `value` set or clear the latch. |

### MedianFilter { #timeseries-kt-medianfilter }

<code class="highlight"><span class="k">class</span> <span class="nf">MedianFilter</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">windowSize</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span><span class="p">)</span> <span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">FloatFilter</span></code>

Rolling median of the last `windowSize` samples. The spike killer: unlike any moving average it removes an isolated outlier completely instead of spreading it over its neighbourhood, and it leaves real edges where they are instead of smearing them into ramps.

| Declaration | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">override</span> <span class="k">fun</span> <span class="nf">invoke</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">value</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span></code> | Records `value` and returns the median of the window, averaging the two middle samples when the count is even. |

### NoiseGate { #timeseries-kt-noisegate }

<code class="highlight"><span class="k">class</span> <span class="nf">NoiseGate</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">threshold</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">attack</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mf">0.01f</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">release</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mf">0.1f</span><span class="p">)</span> <span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">FloatFilter</span></code>

Passes the signal through untouched while it is loud enough and hard-zeroes it when it is not. The gate opens when the tracked envelope rises above `threshold` and closes only once the envelope falls below *half* that, so a signal hovering at the threshold does not flutter.

| Declaration | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">override</span> <span class="k">fun</span> <span class="nf">invoke</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">value</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span></code> | `value` unchanged while the gate is open, `0f` while it is shut — after this sample has updated the envelope. |

### PIDController { #timeseries-kt-pidcontroller }

<code class="highlight"><span class="k">class</span> <span class="nf">PIDController</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">kp</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">ki</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">kd</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span><span class="p">)</span> <span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">FloatFilter</span></code>

A textbook proportional-integral-derivative controller wired up as a filter: it reads the *measured* value and returns the control effort that should push it toward `setpoint`. In a box this is what to reach for when one thing should chase another — a camera trailing a target, a value easing toward the mouse — with overshoot you get to tune rather than inherit.

| Declaration | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">setpoint</span></code> | Where the controller is trying to get the measured value to. Safe to move mid-stream, though the accumulated integral term does not know it moved. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">override</span> <span class="k">fun</span> <span class="nf">invoke</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">value</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span></code> | The control output for a measurement of `value`: `kp·e + ki·Σe + kd·Δe`, where `e = setpoint - value`. |

### CooldownFilter { #timeseries-kt-cooldownfilter }

<code class="highlight"><span class="k">class</span> <span class="nf">CooldownFilter</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">cooldownSamples</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span><span class="p">)</span> <span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">FloatFilter</span></code>

A debouncer for a stream of event flags: it lets a positive sample through, then swallows everything for the next `cooldownSamples` samples. Put it after a detector to turn a burst of flags at one onset into a single flag.

| Declaration | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">override</span> <span class="k">fun</span> <span class="nf">invoke</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">value</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span></code> | `value` itself if it is positive and the cooldown has elapsed, otherwise `0f`. |

### StreamingWhitener { #timeseries-kt-streamingwhitener }

<code class="highlight"><span class="k">class</span> <span class="nf">StreamingWhitener</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">alpha</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mf">0.01f</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">epsilon</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mi">1e</span><span class="p">-</span><span class="mi">5f</span><span class="p">)</span> <span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">FloatFilter</span></code>

A z-score with no window: it tracks the mean and the variance exponentially and returns how far the current sample sits from that running mean, in running standard deviations. The O(1)-memory alternative to [`RollingStats`](math.md#timeseries-kt-rollingstats) plus arithmetic, and the natural pre-stage for anything that wants a roughly zero-mean, unit-variance input.

| Declaration | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">override</span> <span class="k">fun</span> <span class="nf">invoke</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">value</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span></code> | The current sample's distance from the running mean in running standard deviations; 0 on the first call and whenever the signal is flat. |

### BimodalThresholder { #timeseries-kt-bimodalthresholder }

<code class="highlight"><span class="k">class</span> <span class="nf">BimodalThresholder</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">alpha</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mf">0.05f</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">interpolate</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Boolean</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="kc">false</span><span class="p">)</span> <span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">FloatFilter</span></code>

Online two-means clustering of a stream: it keeps two centroids, moves whichever is nearer toward each new sample, and reports which of the two the sample joined. For a signal that really does live at two levels — a switch, a contact sensor, a light that is on or off, a gesture held or not — this finds the two levels for you instead of making you guess a threshold, and it follows them as they drift.

| Declaration | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">override</span> <span class="k">fun</span> <span class="nf">invoke</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">value</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span></code> | `-1f` or `+1f` for the lower or upper cluster — or the interpolated position between the centroids when `interpolate` is set — and `0f` until both centroids have been seeded. |

### PercentileThresholder { #timeseries-kt-percentilethresholder }

<code class="highlight"><span class="k">class</span> <span class="nf">PercentileThresholder</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">windowSize</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mi">100</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">mapToMinusOneToOne</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Boolean</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="kc">true</span><span class="p">)</span> <span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">FloatFilter</span></code>

Reports where the current sample ranks within the last `windowSize` samples: the fraction of the *rest* of the window lying strictly below it. (The current sample is in the window but can never count itself, so the denominator is one less than the fill level and a new high reads exactly 1.0.) Completely distribution-free — no mean, no standard deviation, no fitted law — so a heavy-tailed or lopsided signal cannot mislead it, and one wild outlier moves the output by exactly one rank.

| Declaration | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">override</span> <span class="k">fun</span> <span class="nf">invoke</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">value</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span></code> | The fraction of the rest of the window strictly below `value` — mapped onto `-1..1`, or left as `0..1` when `mapToMinusOneToOne` is false. |

### DynamicRangeCompressor { #timeseries-kt-dynamicrangecompressor }

<code class="highlight"><span class="k">class</span> <span class="nf">DynamicRangeCompressor</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">thresholdDb</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="p">-</span><span class="mi">20f</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">ratio</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mi">4f</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">kneeWidthDb</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mi">10f</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">attackMs</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mi">5f</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">releaseMs</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mi">50f</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">sampleRate</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mi">44100f</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">makeupGainDb</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mi">0f</span><span class="p">)</span> <span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">FloatFilter</span></code>

A proper dB-domain compressor: envelope follower, soft knee, attack and release in milliseconds, makeup gain. Where [`AdaptiveCompander`](math.md#timeseries-kt-adaptivecompander) works in linear amplitude with per-sample coefficients, this one is specified the way a compressor usually is, which makes it the one to use on anything audio-shaped, or on anything whose timing you would rather state in milliseconds than in samples.

| Declaration | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">thresholdDb</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span></code> | Level (dB, full scale = 0) above which gain reduction begins. Negative values are the norm. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">ratio</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span></code> | Compression ratio above the knee: 4 means 4 dB in over threshold yields 1 dB out. 1 is no compression at all. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">kneeWidthDb</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span></code> | Total width (dB) of the soft knee straddling `thresholdDb` — compression eases in across this span instead of switching on abruptly. 0 gives a hard knee. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">attackMs</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span></code> | How quickly (ms) the envelope follows a rising signal. Converted to a per-sample coefficient using `sampleRate`. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">releaseMs</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span></code> | How quickly (ms) the envelope falls after a peak, and so how quickly the gain recovers. Also converted using `sampleRate`. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">sampleRate</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span></code> | The rate (Hz) at which samples arrive, which is what gives `attackMs` and `releaseMs` their meaning. The 44100 default is an audio assumption — set it to your frame rate for a control signal. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">makeupGainDb</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span></code> | Flat gain (dB) applied after the compression, to win back the headroom it just took. Applied at all levels, reduction or not. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">override</span> <span class="k">fun</span> <span class="nf">invoke</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">value</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span></code> | Updates the envelope, reads the knee curve at that level, and returns `value` scaled by the resulting gain plus `makeupGainDb`. |

## units.kt { #units-kt }

Physical units for Field's spreadsheet-style numbers. A [`Quantity`](math.md#units-kt-quantity) pairs a KotUniL
`Expression` (normalized to SI) with the display unit the user actually wrote, so `3 | mm`
still prints as "3 mm".

`withUnit` is what that `| unit` syntax lowers to, and the operator overloads here let a
[`Quantity`](math.md#units-kt-quantity) mix with plain `Number`s and bare `Expression`s in either order under ordinary
dimensional-analysis rules. The rest of the file is presentation: `recognizeDerivedUnit`
matches a dimensional signature against a table of named SI derived units (N, J, W, Pa, Hz, V,
Ω, ...), `autoScaleExpression` chooses an SI prefix, and `formatUnitSuperscripts` rewrites
`kg*m2/s2` as `kg·m²/s²`. `formatExpression` runs those in that order.

The unit algebra itself is KotUniL's, not Field's. Two limits are visible in the code: only
single-factor dimensions are auto-scaled (compound ones like m/s pass through unchanged), and
the derived-unit table is a fixed list, so anything outside it falls back to raw SI symbols.

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/stdlib/units.kt`
